chunks: It is neither dependent on your wishes, nor the wishes of the people of the Book, (but) whosoever does ill will be punished for it, and will find no protector or friend apart from God;
ai.seo_question: What is the basis of divine reward and punishment according to Surah An-Nisa?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to refute the notion that intercession or divine mercy can override the justice of individual deeds, emphasizing that 'wishes' (amānī) of the People of the Book or believers are insufficient without action. It underscores the principle of 'actual recompense' (bi-hā), where every minor or major sin is accounted for, reinforcing the balance between divine justice and mercy. The verse also highlights the isolation of the sinner, who has no protector (wali) or helper (nasir) besides Allah, a concept central to Shia theological discussions on accountability.
